newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia grain harvest so far is at 55.3 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Russia grain harvest so far is at 55.3 mln tonnes.

text.p: Russia's net grain harvest so far is over 55 million tonnes while rains and cold weather are wreaking havoc on Siberian crops, the head of the Agriculture Ministry's crops section, Ivan Gridasov, said on Monday.
In remarks carried by Interfax news agency, Gridasov said unfavourable weather in Siberia had flattened some crops there and caused unthreshed wheat to germinate.
Russia's total harvest was 55.3 million tonnes as of September 14, or 3.7 million tonnes above levels seen at this time last year.
About 69 percent of all grain crops, or 33.3 million ha, had been harvested, which was 2.3 million ha below year-ago levels.
Winter crops to be harvested next year had been sown to nine million ha, a decline of 625,000 ha year-on-year, Gridasov said.
Land already ploughed for spring sowing was 12.7 million ha, compared to 14.2 million ha at this time last year, and only 20 percent of ploughed soil had been fertilised.
Gridasov said seed stocks as of the beginning of this month were 4.5 million tonnes, nearly half of the amount needed, and many central regions did not have enough grain seeds for sowing.
Over one-third of all maize (corn) harvesters, or about 2,200 items, were not in working condition.
